item.content:encoded:
Claves: La rodilla de Freeman, el bate de Ohtani y el cálculo de octubre de Dodgers
CINCINNATI — Freddie Freeman no estuvo en la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para el juego del lunes por la noche contra los Rojos de Cincinnati mientras lidia con molestias en la rodilla derecha.
Aunque el primera base no ha estado en la alineación en tres de los últimos cinco juegos, el mánager Dave Roberts manifestó que poner a Freeman en la lista de lesionados de 10 días para dejarlo listo para la postemporada —algo similar a lo que hicieron con Shohei Ohtani— no es una opción en este momento.
“No creo que (el descanso) tenga que ser de 10 días, pero ¿podría ser más de uno? Esa es una pregunta válida. Tengo que hablar un poco con el cuerpo de preparadores, con Freddie, y al final tomar esa decisión. Pero no creo que la lista de lesionados tenga sentido”, comentó Roberts.
Roberts señaló que no creía que Freeman fuera a tener problemas persistentes con la rodilla durante la postemporada si se puede manejar adecuadamente. Freeman batea para .293, pero está de 3 en sus últimos 30 turnos, con nueve ponches.
Los campeones defensores de la Serie Mundial por segundo año consecutivo llegaron al lunes por la noche con un número mágico de cuatro para asegurar su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en 14 años. Su mayor preocupación es asegurarse de amarrar uno de los dos primeros puestos de preclasificación y un pase directo en la primera ronda.
Los Dodgers (90-59) llegaron al lunes con una ventaja de 2 1/2 juegos sobre Atlanta por el segundo puesto. Milwaukee (93-57) tiene la mejor marca de la Liga Nacional.
“Dado cómo están nuestros muchachos en cuanto a salud, conseguir esa semana sería enorme. Aun así, tenemos que jugar bien para cerrar la temporada y llegar a ese punto”, expresó Roberts.
Ohtani, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho, hará swings desde un tee en Los Ángeles el martes. Serán sus primeros swings desde que ingresó a la lista de lesionados. Roberts indicó que Ohtani ha estado levantando pesas, entrenando y recibiendo tratamiento en los últimos días.
Con Ohtani fuera del viaje de siete juegos, definitivamente ha habido un ambiente distinto en el clubhouse.
“Se siente diferente porque él tiene mucha presencia cuando está en el campo. La última serie no fue indicativa, pero creo que en general estamos jugando buen béisbol. Sabemos que somos mejores con Shohei. Probablemente los aficionados estén decepcionados, pero no creo que nosotros realmente lo hayamos sentido”, dijo Roberts.
La mayor preocupación podría estar con el relevista Edwin Díaz, quien ha permitido seis carreras limpias en 3 1/3 entradas en cuatro apariciones de rehabilitación con Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Díaz no solo está lidiando con una inflamación en el cuello, sino también con problemas de control. Díaz firmó un contrato de 59 millones de dólares por tres años durante la temporada baja y ha tenido dificultades en su primer año en Los Ángeles.
El derecho tendrá otra salida el miércoles, pero Roberts sí dejó abierta la posibilidad de que Díaz quede fuera de los rosters de postemporada.
“Necesita lanzar mejor. No ha sido bueno. La tarjeta de béisbol se ve genial. Pero, tal como estamos, tiene que haber algo a lo que podamos aferrarnos. Y él lo sabe. Quiere lanzar bien”, afirmó Roberts.
__

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Edgardo Henriquez placed on regular season-ending IL appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed right-hander Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort, ending his 2026 regular season. Los Angeles recalled Bobby Miller from Triple-A Oklahoma City as the corresponding roster move.
Henriquez had developed into a regular bullpen option during his first full major league season, making 61 appearances. MLB.com's Sonja Chen took to X, formerly Twitter, shortly after the club announced the transaction and noted the calendar implications of Henriquez's IL placement.
"Henriquez going on the 15-day IL ends his regular season."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Henriquez last pitched Sunday vs. the Miami Marlins, allowing two earned runs on three hits and one walk over two-thirds of an inning. He also recorded one strikeout and received credit for a hold in Los Angeles' 6-4 loss.
The 24-year-old right-hander finishes the regular season with a 4-1 record and 2.85 ERA across 61 games, including one start. The right-hander struck out 71 and walked 25 over 60 innings while posting a 1.03 WHIP. His 61 appearances ranked 24th in the National League.
The timing of the move prevents Henriquez from returning before the regular season concludes September 27. A 15-day placement Monday makes him eligible to return September 29, when the Wild Card Series begins. The move does not automatically rule him out for the postseason if he recovers and earns a roster spot.
The Dodgers have not announced an MRI result, structural diagnosis, or surgery related to Henriquez's back discomfort. His absence removes another pitcher from a Dodgers staff already dealing with multiple injuries, including Shohei Ohtani's right biceps inflammation.
Miller joins the active roster as Los Angeles continues its four-game road series against the Cincinnati Reds. Henriquez's regular season is over, but the Dodgers could still have the right-hander available for the postseason depending on his recovery.

item.title: [Líder en deportes] Edgardo Henriquez a la lista de lesionados
item.dc:creator: Luis Viscaya
item.description: Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles colocaron este lunes en lista de incapacitados a Edgardo Henriquez, las constantes molestias que ha venido sufriendo en su espalda en días recientes el venezolano llevó a los californianos a tomar la decisión. Esta lesión llega en medio de la mejor campaña que ha tenido el diestro desde su debut en Las Mayores en el año 2024. En la presente temporada, el sucrense ha visto acción en 61 encuentros, con marca de 4-1, efectividad de 2.85 y 71 guillotinados en 60.0 episodio
item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles colocaron este lunes en lista de incapacitados a Edgardo Henriquez, las constantes molestias que ha venido sufriendo en su espalda en días recientes el venezolano llevó a los californianos a tomar la decisión.
Esta lesión llega en medio de la mejor campaña que ha tenido el diestro desde su debut en Las Mayores en el año 2024. En la presente temporada, el sucrense ha visto acción en 61 encuentros, con marca de 4-1, efectividad de 2.85 y 71 guillotinados en 60.0 episodios de labor.
El lugar del criollo será ocupado por el también derecho, Bobby Miller, quien fue llamado del Oklahoma City Comets, sucursal AAA de los actuales campeones de la Gran Carpa.
Miller, en 2026 cuenta con récord de 2-0 y un altísimo porcentaje de carreras limpias permitidas de 6.32 en 15.2 entradas.

item.title: [The New York Times] Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, could be left off Dodgers’ postseason roster
item.dc:creator: Fabian Ardaya
item.description: CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers set out this winter to address the closer position for good. Instead, they’re facing the possibility that a reliever they signed as a star free agent will be excluded from their postseason plans for a second consecutive season. Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, as Tanner Scott did a year ago, and his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City has gone poorly enough that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Monday the club could leave the three-time All
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers set out this winter to address the closer position for good. Instead, they’re facing the possibility that a reliever they signed as a star free agent will be excluded from their postseason plans for a second consecutive season.
Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, as Tanner Scott did a year ago, and his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City has gone poorly enough that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Monday the club could leave the three-time All-Star closer off the postseason roster. Against minor-leaguers Sunday, Díaz surrendered five runs, walked three, hit a batter and recorded just two outs in his worst appearance yet.
Advertisement
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said. “So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
The Dodgers gave Díaz three years and $69 million to address a bullpen that floundered in 2025. They won their second consecutive World Series despite Scott — who signed a four-year, $72 million contract — not appearing in a single playoff game.
A second plunge into the deep end of the relief market brought even worse results than the 4.74 ERA and league-worst 10 blown saves Scott had in 2025. Díaz’s famous trumpets have sounded more like a sad trombone.
Díaz’s 16 appearances with the Dodgers yielded a disastrous 11.85 ERA. He missed three months due to arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies in his right elbow. Upon his return, he struggled enough that the Dodgers almost immediately put him back on the injured list for what they called a neck issue. They believed his struggles were mechanical, citing the lowest arm angle of his career (14.9 degrees) as a reason his stuff and command were nowhere near where they needed to be.
Attempts to correct the issue have not worked. What was supposed to be a pair of rehab outings has been extended. The organization thought Sunday’s outing could be the final step before activation, with Díaz joining the team in Cincinnati this week to try to re-earn his closer’s job.
But Díaz has allowed six runs and walked seven of the 21 batters he’s faced since starting his rehab. Even more concerning is how Díaz’s delivery seems even more out of whack than before. His fastball still lacks the north-south movement that it needs to succeed. On that pitch this season, he’s averaged 11.8 inches of induced vertical break, which measures how much “hop” or “ride” the pitch generates. The 15 fastballs he threw Sunday generated just 9.7 inches of IVB.
There’s plenty for Díaz to fix, and not a lot of time.
Advertisement
“He needs to pitch better,” Roberts said. “I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But it’s like, where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well.”
So the Dodgers summoned rehabbing reliever Kris Bubic to join the big club Monday instead. Bubic is expected to pitch as soon as Wednesday, Roberts said. Bubic, a former All-Star starting pitcher with the Kansas City Royals, was acquired at the trade deadline and has thrown 5 2/3 scoreless innings with nine strikeouts on his rehab assignment since the trade.
Díaz will stick with Oklahoma City for at least one more outing on Wednesday, and the organization will evaluate from there, Roberts said.
The Dodgers will spend the coming days trying to sort out how they will attack the ninth inning. One option went on the IL on Monday, when the Dodgers placed hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the shelf with a lower back issue; Henriquez has been the Dodgers’ most effective reliever recently, with a 1.69 ERA since Aug. 5. Now, his regular season is over.
Scott, who has bounced back this year with a 2.91 ERA, will be part of fixing the ninth-inning problem they thought they’d avoid entirely when they signed Díaz.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki gets encouraging injury recovery from Dave Roberts appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki took an encouraging step Monday in his recovery from a right middle-finger blister, throwing a bullpen session ahead of the club's four-game road series against the Cincinnati Reds beginning Monday. The development keeps the 24-year-old in consideration for a return Thursday vs. the Reds, though the Dodgers have not committed to activating him. The Los Angeles Times' Maddie Lee took to X, formerly Twitter, on Monday afternoon with manager Dave Roberts' latest update.
"Roki Sasaki threw a bullpen today and tested out covering the blister wirh dermabond, Dave Roberts said. He's a possibility for Thursday, but 'we just can't put him in a position to go backwards,' so still TBD."
The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since August 27 after the blister opened during his start against the Atlanta Braves one day earlier. He lasted 3 1/3 innings and threw 66 pitches before leaving the game.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Monday's bullpen allowed Sasaki to test Dermabond over the healing blister while throwing. The Dodgers remain cautious because another setback could further delay his return as the regular season enters its final weeks.
Sasaki is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA and 117 strikeouts across 119 1/3 innings and 23 starts this season. His results had improved before the injury, as he posted a 3.05 ERA over 38 1/3 innings in seven starts following the All-Star break.
Thursday remains a possible return date rather than a confirmed activation. The Dodgers have an open rotation spot for the series finale against Cincinnati, but Sasaki's availability will depend on how his finger responds following Monday's bullpen session.
The Dogers head into Monday at 90-59 and atop the NL West as it prepares for the postseason. Getting Sasaki healthy would provide another rotation option, but Roberts' update makes clear that the club will not risk reversing his progress simply to fill Thursday's opening.
Related: Dodgers tie historic streak with Reds series opener takedown
Related: Tarik Skubal helps Dodgers clinch 14th-straight playoff berth

item.title: [MLB.com] Freeman (knee soreness) out of lineup again, though likely to avoid IL
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: CINCINNATI -- Freddie Freeman was out of the Dodgers' starting lineup for Monday night's series opener against the Reds at Great American Ball Park as the star first baseman continues to manage soreness in his right knee, which he has described as patellar tendinitis. It marked the third time in the Dodgers' past five games that Freeman was not in the starting nine. Manager Dave Roberts reaffirmed that he does not believe Freeman will go on the injured list, and he's expected to return to the li
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Freddie Freeman was out of the Dodgers' starting lineup for Monday night's series opener against the Reds at Great American Ball Park as the star first baseman continues to manage soreness in his right knee, which he has described as patellar tendinitis.
It marked the third time in the Dodgers' past five games that Freeman was not in the starting nine. Manager Dave Roberts reaffirmed that he does not believe Freeman will go on the injured list, and he's expected to return to the lineup on Tuesday.
"I just think right now, with where we’re at in the season, an IL is not an option in the sense of -- I personally don’t think we have a better option," Roberts said. "I don’t think it needs to be 10 days. But could it be more than one? That’s a fair question."
Freeman is essentially day to day moving forward. Roberts believes that Freeman's knee has impacted his offensive performance lately, as the 37-year-old is hitting 3-for-30 (.100) with just one extra-base hit in September.
There is some evidence that the knee has been hindering Freeman for longer, as his power numbers have dropped off over the past couple months. He only has one home run in his past 55 games, and he's slugging .350 in that span.
For most of his power drought, Freeman was still hitting for average and consistently getting on base. But when his overall performance took a dip earlier this month, the Dodgers opted to rest him, knowing how important he will be to their offense in the postseason. Freeman is hitting .293 with an .818 OPS in 142 games this season.
Roberts is hopeful that giving Freeman time off now will make it less likely that he'll have to manage his knee throughout the postseason.
"I think that if we can kind of manage it … depending on how the season goes, as far as the recovery," Roberts said. "And then also in the postseason, there’s more off-days. So I think that just trying to get ahold of it, I think that’s the main thing."
The Dodgers' lineup is far from full strength in mid-September, with a dozen regular-season games remaining. Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day IL due to lingering right biceps and left knee issues and won't be eligible to be activated until Sept. 23. Andy Pages is working his way back from a fracture in his left hand and is also unlikely to return until the final week.
Freeman isn't the only active Dodger who is banged up. Miguel Rojas, who exited early on Sunday after aggravating his right shoulder, was back in the starting lineup on Monday. Rojas is sore but playable, so he'll start against the Reds' left-handed starters this week in Cincinnati.
It's commonly said that every player is dealing with some kind of physical issue, big or small, at this point in the season. Not only have the injuries piled up for the Dodgers of late, but they have affected some of their most important hitters.
But for the Dodgers, who entered Monday a win away from clinching their 14th consecutive postseason berth, the rest of the regular season is less consequential than the games that come after. They will use these final two weeks -- and if they finish with a top-two record in the NL, the bye week -- to get their injured players right in time for the postseason.
"Honestly, I think right now it's front of mind, it's not great," Roberts said. "But I will say this: Once you get to October, athletes have a magical way of feeling better. It happens every single year, where there's that extra adrenaline that athletes get when you get to the postseason.”

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani se ha perdido seis de los últimos siete partidos de Los Angeles Dodgers debido a las lesiones que ha venido arrastrando esta temporada. La primera fue en la rodilla, una molestia que lo alejó del montículo desde principios de julio y que, con poco tiempo para recuperarse antes de los playoffs, hace casi un hecho que no vuelva a lanzar en 2026. Una baja sensible para los Dodgers en el tramo más importante de la campaña, en el que buscan conquistar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva.
Shohei Ohtani to be placed on the injured list (left knee, right biceps), Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announces. pic.twitter.com/AG3VlX3TVe
— MLB (@MLB) September 10, 2026
La segunda lesión que sufrió esta temporada fue en el bíceps, una molestia que ha ido empeorando con el paso de las semanas. Ohtani comenzó a sufrir molestias en el cuello como consecuencia de este problema, lo que obligó a los Dodgers a colocarlo en la lista de lesionados y provocó que se perdiera los últimos encuentros. La buena noticia es que el japonés ha estado trabajando para regresar en este cierre de temporada regular y volver a ocupar su puesto como bateador designado de cara a los playoffs de la MLB.
Ohtani será fundamental en las aspiraciones de los Dodgers
Previo al inicio de la serie ante los Reds en Cincinnati, el mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, confirmó que Ohtani tiene programado realizar swings desde un tee antes del partido del martes. La actividad representa un paso adelante en su recuperación y mantiene abierta la posibilidad de que pueda regresar a tiempo para ayudar a Los Angeles en los playoffs.
"I think it's important that he does pitch because he has the ability to do it. He's elite."@spillygoat19 shares his thoughts on whether or not he would discourage Shohei Ohtani from pitching in the future.
MLB Network + @NewBalance pic.twitter.com/KqBg6i0pMd
Por fortuna, los Dodgers se prepararon durante la temporada ante una eventual ausencia prolongada de su superestrella. Por esa razón, adquirieron al pitcher Tarik Skubal antes de la fecha límite de intercambios para fortalecer una rotación de lanzadores que buscará llegar en las mejores condiciones a la postemporada.
Shohei Ohtani could resume swinging Monday or Tuesday as he continues recovering from lingering right biceps and left knee issues.
Ohtani is eligible to return from the IL on September 23, giving him a short window to prepare for the postseason.#Dodgers #BlueDynasty pic.twitter.com/l2vdNja7kE
Además, los Dodgers llamó a uno de los mejores prospectos de las Grandes Ligas, Josue De Paula, para aportar a la ofensiva mientras Ohtani se recupera. El pelotero impresionó en sus primeros partidos ante los Marlins, una actuación que le permite a los Dodgers darle mayor tiempo de recuperación a Ohtani con la esperanza de que esté listo para disputar el Clásico de Otoño.

item.content:encoded:
One day after allowing his first runs in four weeks, Dodgers reliever Edgardo Henríquez was placed on the 15-day injured list with lower back discomfort. His regular season is over.
Henríquez has been one of the best relievers on the team this season, with a 2.85 ERA and 2.47 xERA in 61 games, with 71 strikeouts and 25 walks in 60 innings, with a 29.3-percent strikeout rate and only one home run allowed. The 24-year-old leads the Dodgers bullpen in innings and xERA, and is second only to Tanner Scott in strikeouts.
Sunday was a rare rough outing for Henríquez, who allowed three hits, a walk, and two runs in the eighth inning, recording only two outs. Those were the first runs allowed by Henríquez since August 16, snapping a string of 11 consecutive scoreless appearances.
“It’s the confidence he has in his fastball. Everybody knows it’s not easy to hit 103, 104 coming at you with confidence,” outfielder Teoscar Hernández said last week on the Dodgers’ homestand. “That’s been the difference between the Edgardo we saw at the beginning of the year, and the Edgardo we’re seeing right now.”
Whether Henriquez will be ready and available once the postseason starts remains to be seen.
With Henríquez sidelined, Bobby Miller was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. Miller was just optioned last Monday, but he’s able to return before his 15 days are up because he’s replacing an injured player.
Miller pitched once for Oklahoma City after getting optioned, and it was a rough outing, with five runs allowed in 1 2/3 innings on Friday against Sugar Land, with all five runs scored on two home runs by the same player.

Los Angeles Dodgers Dropping Max Muncy to Seventh in Batting Order Muncy is b
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up to face the Cincinnati Reds for the first game of their four-game series on Monday.
The Dodgers are entering this game cold, as they lost each of their last two games. Yet, they will now be looking to get things back on track against Cincinnati from here.
As Los Angeles prepares for their series against the Reds, they have announced a significant lineup change regarding Max Muncy.
Los Angeles Dodgers Dropping Max Muncy to Seventh in Batting Order
Muncy is being dropped to seventh in the Dodgers’ batting order for Monday’s game against the Reds. This is after he batted third against the Marlins in their Sunday matchup.
Muncy will also be switching to third base after being Los Angeles’ DH in their last game.
The Dodgers’ batting order for their game against the Marlins is as follows:
T. Edman CF
M. Betts SS
W. Smith C
K. Tucker RF
T. Hernández LF
M. Rojas 2B
M. Muncy 3B
E. Hernández 1B
J. De Paula DH
Looking at Muncy
Muncy dropping to seventh in Los Angeles’ batting order comes after he went 0-for-4 against the Marlins on Sunday, with two strikeouts.
While Muncy struggled last game, he certainly could bounce back against the Reds. Before his hitless performance against the Marlins, he had hits in each of his previous six games. With that, don’t be surprised if he has a strong bounce-back game for Los Angeles on Monday.
Muncy has 28 home runs, 71 RBI, and a .254 batting average in 137 games this season with the Dodgers. He has been a big part of the Dodgers’ offense this season, just like he has been for years now.

Paul Gervase was called up from Triple-A to give the Dodgers an extra arm in the bullpen, after the Dodgers used four relievers Friday, three on Saturday, and four more on Sunday against the Marlins. item.content:encoded:
The fresh arm express continues to run in September, with Emmet Sheehan optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City ahead of Monday night's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park, one day after he pitched six scoreless innings on Sunday in Miami.
Paul Gervase was called up from Triple-A to give the Dodgers an extra arm in the bullpen, after the Dodgers used four relievers Friday, three on Saturday, and four more on Sunday against the Marlins. Monday is the fourth day of a stretch of 10 game days in a row for the Dodgers, their final extended stretch of games this season.
This had nothing to do with Sheehan's performance, as he allowed only one run in 11 2/3 innings last week after getting called back up from Oklahoma City himself, with 15 strikeouts. But Sheehan is on the outside looking in when it comes to the Dodgers' postseason rotation, and the team might also get Roki Sasaki at some point this week from a blister on his right middle finger.
Gervase last pitched on Friday for Oklahoma City, striking out four in a four-out save in a scoreless outing to close out a win over Sugar Land. On the season, the 6'10 right-hander had a 4.56 ERA and five saves in 38 games in Triple-A, with 66 strikeouts and 35 walks in 47 1/3 innings.
This is the fifth stint in the majors this season for Gervase, who has a 2.35 ERA in four appearances for the Dodgers, with eight strikeouts and five walks in 7 2/3 innings.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Demote Red-Hot Starting Pitcher in Surprise Move
item.dc:creator: Noah Camras; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have optioned right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan to Triple-A in a surprise move ahead of Monday's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds. Sheehan has been dominant over his last two starts since returning to the MLB level, allowing a combined one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts. He pitched six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins on Sunday. However, the Dodgers wanted to bring up a fresh bullpen arm for the beginning of their four-game series in Cincinn
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have optioned right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan to Triple-A in a surprise move ahead of Monday's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds.
Sheehan has been dominant over his last two starts since returning to the MLB level, allowing a combined one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts. He pitched six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins on Sunday.
However, the Dodgers wanted to bring up a fresh bullpen arm for the beginning of their four-game series in Cincinnati. Thus, Sheehan was the odd man out, with right-handed pitcher Paul Gervase being called up.
Dodgers Option Emmet Sheehan
Sheehan has had a rollercoaster 2026 season that began with much promise. However, the right-hander struggled across his first 20 starts, and was optioned to Triple-A on Aug. 3 after allowing five runs on six hits over 2.2 innings against the Boston Red Sox.
At the time of the demotion, Sheehan's ERA was 5.29. However, he played well across four Triple-A outings and earned another opportunity at the MLB level on Sept. 7 against the Reds.
Sheehan allowed one run over 5.2 innings with a tied-for-career-high 10 strikeouts against Cincinnati. That led to him staying in the rotation for another turn, where he dominated the Marlins on Sunday.
Sheehan is now ineligible to return to the Dodgers before the end of the regular season barring an injury to someone else that would allow him to be called back up.
He'll look to continue to keep his game strong ahead of the postseason, where he could still factor into the team's plans.
“There was a lot of stuff, going down and trying to figure things out in a less stressful place which was nice,” Sheehan said after his start on Sept. 7. “Just getting my delivery locked in and really just making sure I’m hammering it during the week so I can just go out there and compete which I felt I was doing tonight.”
"I’ve been optioned before," he added. "It’s always, 'See what we can do down there, and see what we can do to bring it back up here.'"
Now, he'll have to do that once more.
Dodgers Calling Up Paul Gervase
As for Gervase, the right-hander has made four appearances for the Dodgers at the big league level this season, allowing two runs over 7.2 innings for a 2.35 ERA with eight strikeouts.
Across 38 appearances at Triple-A Oklahoma City, he has a 4.56 ERA with 66 strikeouts over 47.1 innings.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– With his already career-worst season reaching nightmarish new depths, Kyle Tucker was pulled aside recently by Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
The topic of conversation: The $240 million outfielder’s playing time over the rest of the season.
Externally, of course, calls had been mounting for Tucker to be platooned, if not outright benched, as his numbers continued to plummet amid an ongoing second-half slump.
Internally, however, the Dodgers had decided to double down on their faith in this offseason’s marquee free-agent signing.
Thus, the message Roberts delivered was simple.
“I told him, I’m gonna ride or die with him,” Roberts shared this weekend.
In that exact phrasing?
“I did,” Roberts joked. “That was my young term phrase.”
On this day, Roberts had reason to laugh. The previous two games, Tucker had finally offered signs of life at the plate, posting back-to-back performances with three hits and a home run. Over the last week, Dodgers hitting coaches believed they had finally found a breakthrough with the left-handed slugger’s swing, one that (at least temporarily) cleaned up some mechanical flaws that had hampered him all year.
Alas, in Tucker’s 2026 campaign, no turnaround was ever going to be that simple.
Over the two games since, he has gone 0-for-8 again, including a strikeout with the bases loaded in the top of the ninth on Sunday. On the season, his numbers remain unthinkably disappointing, with a batting average of .226, an OPS of .692 and an almost negligible 0.3 mark in wins above replacement.
At this point, it is all adding up to a lost season for the 29-year-old, who is threatening to become one of the biggest free-agent flops in at least the sport’s recent high-priced history.
And yet, the Dodgers aren’t wavering from their commitment to keep playing the four-time All-Star, rolling the dice “talent level” and “proven track record,” as Roberts cited, by keeping him in the lineup for the long haul.
“I was prepared, the organization was prepared, to give him as much leash as we possibly could to work through some things, and I do think that now we’re starting to see the fruits,” Roberts said. “So I see no other reason why we would pivot from running him out there every day.”
The only caveat Roberts offered: “I guess, to that same point, until you can’t, right?”
Trying to identify the root cause of Tucker’s dismal season has been about as easy as discerning his emotions through his stoic and reserved facade.
The one thing everyone has agreed on: “It’s purely mechanical,” as co-hitting coach Robert Van Scoyoc told the California Post recently. “His swing plane is pretty unique, but it’s just not working the way that it used to.”
The problem, as Tucker himself conceded last month, has been finding an answer or adjustment that works.
“I feel like I’ve tried just about everything,” he said. “And every time I feel like I’m turning a corner, I get hit with a roadblock.”
Tucker’s swing has always been atypical, both in the way he “lays the bat back” in his stance (which, according to fellow hitting coach Aaron Bates, leads to a longer path in which “his margin for error is a little smaller”) and how he strides through the ball (launching off his back foot with an almost Scottie Scheffler-esque follow-through).
When it’s all synced up, it makes him one of the most consistent hitters in the game; reminiscent to some evaluators of a modern-day Ted Williams.
But when it’s not…
“I think it’s a slippery slope,” Bates said.
Only now, the Dodgers are hoping they have found a way to potentially end the slide.
For much of the year, Bates said Tucker was struggling to replicate his old, inside-out swing path. Instead, he was “cutting down and across the ball,” preventing him from squaring up heaters or adjusting to off-speed pitches. According to MLB’s Statcast system, his rate of “barreled” balls has fallen almost in half as a result, from 10.8% last year (and 12.9% in 2024) to 6.3% this season.
Their initial attempt at a fix was having Tucker cycle through old drills and mental cues he had used in his career previously. Only this time, those old band-aids failed to make a difference, leaving a player who once always had offensive answers toiling with only growing mechanical questions.
Why that is still confounds the Dodgers. Theories have ranged from a slow adjustment to his new surroundings, to potential lingering side effects from the hand fracture he played through last season with the Chicago Cubs.
“It definitely seems like things kind of shifted after [that],” Van Scoyoc said, noting that Tucker also struggled down the stretch in 2025. “So it could be that, but it might not be. We don’t exactly know.”
What was clear was the need to try something different. Thus, there has been constant trial-and-error in Tucker’s elongated batting-cage sessions of late.
Last week, something finally clicked. As Bates described it, Tucker found comfort with the thought of a “no-roll swing” –– where instead of flipping his hands at the end of his follow-through, he keeps them more square to the big part of the field.
“Guys who throw right-handed but hit lefty, it’s something they struggle with sometimes, because the right side of their body is the dominant side,” Bates said, noting that the team has made similar adjustments with Tommy Edman, Alex Freeland and Dalton Rushing this season.
In Tucker’s case, the cue helped flatten his swing.
“He was missing pitches he thought he needed to get on top of,” Bates said, “and needed to think about swinging high instead of swinging down.” It has also kept his barrel in the zone longer, allowing him to re-adjust to off-speed offerings (one of his great strengths as a hitter for most of his career) while better squaring mistakes left over the plate (like the hanging inside sweeper he belted for a grand slam on Friday).
“There’s a lot more room for error hitting the ball, because you can hit it deep and go the other way or catch it out in front and pull it a little bit more,” Tucker explained. “Just trying to be consistent with that and be as long through the zone as possible.”
Whether it proves to be a genuine breakthrough, or just another false start in a season that’s never gotten going, the Dodgers are willing to keep taking the time to find out.
After all, while Tucker’s regular season is beyond salvaging, Van Scoyoc maintained that “he can find it in one swing and then go on a run.”
Thus, they will “ride or die” with him the rest of the way, despite the dismal struggles the last five months have wrought.
“I mean, the numbers probably are what they are, but we’ve got a lot of important games coming next month,” Tucker said, eyeing what he hopes will be validation in the playoffs. “That’s the most important thing … As long as you win the game and kind of contribute to that in some way, that’s all you can really try and do.”
Added Roberts: “If you perform at the right time, all is forgotten.”

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are one win away from clinching a National League playoff berth. Ahead of tonight’s game, the Dodgers make a couple changes in their lineup, one of them involving utility player Tommy Edman. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are one win away from clinching a National League playoff berth.
Monday, September 14, the Dodgers begin a three-game series against the Cincinnati Reds for the second time seven games.
Ahead of tonight’s game, the Dodgers make a couple changes in their lineup, one of them involving utility player Tommy Edman.
Tommy Edman is Back in the Lineup vs. the Reds After a Rest Day on Sunday
Per Los Angeles Dodgers reporter David Vassegh, the team announced their starting lineup against the Cincinnati Reds on Monday.
#Dodgers Lineup vs #Reds LHP, Nick Lodolo: Edman CF, Betts SS, Smith C, Tucker RF, T. Hernandez LF, Rojas 2B, Muncy 3B, E. Hernandez 1B, JDP DH, Tarik Skubal SP,” Vassegh wrote on X.
Edman sat out in Sunday’s loss against the Miami Marlins because Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, did not want him playing all three games on a turf field.
“#Dodgers Dave Roberts originally said Josue De Paula would DH all 3 games in Miami,” Dodgers insider Bill Plunket wrote on X ahead of Sunday’s game. “Thought it thru and decided he didn’t want Teoscar Hernandez or Tommy Edman to play all 3 games on turf here. So De Paula gets the start in LF.”
Edman and the Dodgers have been carefully monitoring the center fielder’s ankle, after spending nearly half the season on the injured list. The 31-year-old underwent an offseason ankle surgery and did not return to the Dodgers lineup until June 17.
While the Dodgers primary center fielder Andy Pages, remains on the injured list, Edman has spent most of starts in center.
Despite slashing .257/.339/.390 in 72 games, Edman’s seven game stretch shows signs of a quite the slump.
He’s batting .091 with five strikeouts, two hits, and two RBIs in his last 22 at-bats. Both of hits coming against the Washington Nationals on September 6.
Hopefully yesterday’s much needed rest day gets Edman back where he needs to be.
Los Angeles Dodgers Magic Number to Win NL West is Four
There only 15 days until the first MLB postseason game, and 13 games left in the season for the Dodgers. They can clinch a postseason berth tonight with a win against the Reds.
“LAD can clinch a postseason berth today with a win at Cincinnati *or* losses by both the Padres (@ COL) AND the Diamondbacks (v. MIA),” Dodgers beat writer Katie Woo wrote on X.
For the National League West, the Dodgers’ magic number is four.
After their series concludes against the Reds, the Dodgers are strictly facing NL West opponents. Two series at-home against the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres, and rounding off the season on the road to face San Francisco for the final time in 2026.

item.title: [Diario Libre] De Brooklyn a Santo Domingo y de Doble-A a los Dodgers: la ruta de Josué De Paula
item.dc:creator: Omar Santana

item.content:encoded:
El jardinero de 21 años abandonó Nueva York durante la pandemia para intentar firmar como profesional en República Dominicana. Los Dodgers lo contrataron por US$397,500 y cuatro años después se saltó Triple-A para llegar a Grandes Ligas.
El primer hit de Josué De Paula en las Grandes Ligas no fue un sencillo para guardar discretamente en una vitrina. Fue un cuadrangular de tres carreras.
El domingo, en Miami, el joven jardinero de los Dodgers encontró una recta de Eury Pérez y la envió al segundo nivel del jardín derecho del loanDepot park. La pelota recorrió unos 416 pies y salió del bate a 108.2 millas por hora. Más tarde agregó un doble y terminó de 2-2 en la derrota 6-4 de Los Ángeles ante los Marlins.
Era apenas su tercer día como jugador de Grandes Ligas.
La imagen resume una historia que comenzó de manera poco convencional. De Paula nació el 24 de mayo de 2005 en Brooklyn, Nueva York. Creció en Estados Unidos, asistió a Benjamin N. Cardozo High School, en Queens, y pertenece a una familia con antecedentes deportivos: es primo segundo de los exjugadores de la NBA Stephon Marbury y Sebastian Telfair.
Pero su camino hacia el béisbol profesional no pasó inicialmente por el sistema estadounidense de escuelas secundarias, universidades y draft.
Pasó por República Dominicana.
La pandemia cambió el camino
De Paula apenas había disputado su primer partido de béisbol con Cardozo cuando la pandemia de COVID-19 paralizó el deporte escolar en 2020.
Durante ese período, según relató posteriormente el propio jugador, su padre le planteó una alternativa: trasladarse a República Dominicana y tratar de abrirse paso por la ruta que cada año siguen cientos de prospectos latinoamericanos que entrenan para conseguir contratos con organizaciones de Grandes Ligas.
La familia se trasladó al país en 2021. De Paula tenía 15 años.
En Santo Domingo entrenó en El Niche Baseball Academy. El cambio era considerable: había nacido y crecido en Nueva York, pero entraba ahora al competitivo sistema dominicano de desarrollo de prospectos internacionales.
La apuesta tardó apenas unos meses en producir resultados.
US$397,500 y una firma que terminó pareciendo barata
El 15 de enero de 2022, cuando tenía 16 años, De Paula firmó con los Dodgers como agente libre internacional por un bono de US$397,500. Aunque nació en Estados Unidos, fue captado y firmado desde República Dominicana.
No era el nombre principal de aquella clase internacional de Los Ángeles. Los Dodgers anunciaron alrededor de 30 firmas y la atención se concentraba entonces sobre todo en otros prospectos de mayor cotización.
Con el tiempo, esos US$397,500 comenzaron a parecer una inversión muy favorable para la organización.
Su primera prueba profesional ocurrió precisamente en el país donde había buscado la firma.
En 2022 jugó para DSL Dodgers Bautista en la Dominican Summer League. Bateó .349, tuvo porcentaje de embazarse de .448 y slugging de .522 en 53 partidos, con cinco jonrones, 30 carreras impulsadas, 42 anotadas y 16 bases robadas. Fue seleccionado al equipo Todos Estrellas de postemporada de la liga.
El experimento dominicano había funcionado.
El difícil salto a Estados Unidos
En 2023 comenzó el recorrido por el sistema de ligas menores de Estados Unidos con Rancho Cucamonga, sucursal Clase A de los Dodgers.
Allí apareció una de las características que después llamaría la atención de la organización: su capacidad de controlar la zona de strike. En 74 partidos bateó .284, llegó a base a ritmo de .396 y produjo 40 carreras. El poder, sin embargo, todavía no había llegado: solo conectó dos cuadrangulares.
El crecimiento se hizo más evidente en 2024.
Entre Rancho Cucamonga y Great Lakes jugó 107 encuentros y terminó con promedio de .268, OBP de .404, 10 jonrones, 62 remolcadas y 27 bases robadas. Además negoció 84 transferencias, una cifra que reflejaba su disciplina en el plato a una edad en la que muchos prospectos todavía dependen casi exclusivamente de sus condiciones físicas.
Durante una de esas temporadas muertas entrenó en Miami junto a Juan Soto y Elly De La Cruz. La atención comenzó a trasladarse hacia el desarrollo de poder en un cuerpo de 6 pies y 3 pulgadas.
Los Dodgers empezaron a hablar de él en términos poco habituales. Dentro de la organización llegó a ser considerado uno de los bateadores jóvenes más avanzados desarrollados por el club en años recientes.
El jonrón que lo puso delante de todos
La explosión mediática llegó en julio.
De Paula fue seleccionado para el Juego de Futuras Estrellas y encontró a dos corredores en circulación frente al zurdo Noah Schultz, otro de los principales prospectos de MLB.
Conectó un slider y mandó la pelota 416 pies por el jardín derecho-central. El batazo salió a 108.5 millas por hora, dio ventaja 3-2 a la Liga Nacional y terminó convirtiéndolo en el Jugador Más Valioso del partido.
Era el primer prospecto de los Dodgers que recibía ese reconocimiento desde Chin-Lung Hu en 2007. Entre los dominicanos que lo habían ganado anteriormente estaban Alfonso Soriano y José Reyes.
Su temporada terminó con 12 cuadrangulares y 32 robos. Tras 98 encuentros con Great Lakes recibió finalmente el ascenso a Doble-A Tulsa, pero allí tuvo un aterrizaje abrupto: se fue sin hits en 18 turnos durante cuatro partidos.
Fue una pausa, no un techo.
¿Jugó con el Escogido?
De Paula pertenece a los Leones del Escogido.
El equipo lo seleccionó en la tercera ronda del Sorteo de Novatos de Lidom de 2023, cuando todavía era un jugador de Clase A de los Dodgers.
Sin embargo, en las fuentes oficiales y registros revisados no aparece evidencia de que haya disputado hasta ahora un partido oficial de temporada regular con los Leones. Es decir, sus derechos en el béisbol otoño-invernal dominicano pertenecen al Escogido, pero su desarrollo competitivo se ha mantenido dentro del sistema de los Dodgers.
El año que abrió la puerta
En 2026 regresó a Tulsa y convirtió Doble-A en su plataforma de lanzamiento.
En 124 partidos bateó .303, con .401 de porcentaje de embasarse y .547 de slugging. Disparó 27 jonrones, produjo 104 carreras y robó 31 bases. En toda su trayectoria de ligas menores acumuló 460 partidos con línea ofensiva de .286/.404/.453, 56 cuadrangulares y 280 impulsadas.
Ascenso a Grandes Ligas
También mejoró una variable que suele determinar si un bateador joven puede trasladar su producción a las Mayores: redujo su porcentaje de ponches mientras aumentaba considerablemente el poder.
En los entrenamientos de primavera ya había dado señales. Bateó .375 en 14 encuentros y volvió a participar en el Juego de Futuras Estrellas durante el verano.
Todavía faltaba un escalón: Triple-A.
Los Dodgers decidieron saltárselo.
De Doble-A directamente a sustituir a Ohtani
La oportunidad apareció cuando Los Ángeles colocó a Shohei Ohtani en la lista de lesionados.
El 11 de septiembre, los Dodgers seleccionaron el contrato de De Paula desde Tulsa. Para incorporarlo al roster de 40 jugadores trasladaron al lanzador Eric Lauer a la lista de lesionados de 60 días.
El movimiento resultó especialmente significativo: De Paula se convirtió en el primer jugador de posición de los Dodgers en saltar directamente de Doble-A a Grandes Ligas en más de una década.
Ni siquiera él esperaba que ocurriera de esa manera.
Cuando el dirigente de Tulsa, Eric Wedge, lo llamó a su oficina y le informó que tomaría un avión para reunirse con "los muchachos grandes", De Paula contó que inicialmente no entendió hacia dónde lo estaban enviando. Pensaba que Triple-A era el paso siguiente.
El viernes 11 de septiembre apareció como bateador designado y séptimo en la alineación contra Miami. Tenía 21 años y 110 días, convirtiéndose en uno de los Dodgers más jóvenes en debutar durante los últimos años. No consiguió hit en tres turnos, pero recibió una transferencia.
Dos días después ocupó por primera vez los jardines.
Y entonces llegó Eury Pérez.
De Paula conectó su primer hit de Grandes Ligas, un jonrón de tres carreras, y luego agregó un doble. Cuatro años y ocho meses después de firmar por US$397,500 en República Dominicana, el muchacho que salió de Brooklyn durante una pandemia y volvió al Caribe buscando una oportunidad ya estaba produciendo carreras para los Dodgers en septiembre.
La lesión de Ohtani abrió la puerta. Sus cuatro años atravesando la Dominican Summer League, Clase A, Clase A Avanzada y Doble-A explican por qué los Dodgers decidieron que no necesitaba tocar ninguna otra antes de entrar.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers bullpen implodes yet again, squander chance at playoff berth

item.content:encoded:
MIAMI –– The Dodgers’ bullpen melted down once again on Sunday in Miami.
Only this time, they got an unhelpful hand from some shaky late-game defense.
In a 6-4 loss to the Miami Marlins, the Dodgers allowed all of the scoring in the final two innings of what became a walk-off defeat; watching three high-leverage relievers –– Edgardo Henriquez, Tanner Scott and Brock Stewart –– falter after their infield gave away extra outs behind them.
In Henriquez’s two-run eighth inning, one would-be groundout instead snuck between shortstop Mookie Betts and second baseman Miguel Rojas, leaving Rojas injured after he made a late sliding attempt. Another got stuck in Betts’ hand while he tried to make a charging throw on the run, gifting the Marlins a free scoring opportunity that would lead to a two-run single from Otto Lopez.
The four-run ninth inning, which was capped off by Agustín Ramírez’s walk-off homer against Stewart, was just as frustrating, as Scott’s bid for a four-out save imploded after a pair of infield singles; one on a bunt, and another on a bad underhand flipped from a hobbled Freddie Freeman at first base.
“When you give a team extra outs,” manager Dave Roberts said, “that’s what happens.”
Initially, it appeared as though the Dodgers might still escape.
After Lopez’s single in the eighth, Scott replaced Henriquez to face Griffin Conine and struck him out on three pitches to end the inning and keep a 3-2 lead intact.
In the top of the ninth, the Dodgers added to the advantage on Betts’ RBI double, giving them “enough to win” offensively, as Roberts put it, even though they left the bases loaded later in the frame.
Alas, the bottom of the ninth immediately went sideways on an Xavier Edwards ground ball to lead off the inning.
Freeman, who has been playing through a knee injury and is mired in a 1-for-26 slump, fielded the ball but made a bad underhand flip back to first. Scott had to adjust to it as he went to cover the base, and was too late to recover as Edwards beat the play out.
Jakob Marsee came up next and executed a perfect bunt inside the third-base line.
Then, Javier Sanoja got jammed by a slider but still muscled a two-run double into the left-field corner.
Just like that, the Dodgers’ lead was gone. It was only Scott’s fourth blown save in 26 opportunities this season, but also the sixth time in his last 11 outings he has given up a run.
“Actually, I think the last week has been really good as far as the stuff,” Roberts said when asked of that trend, which has pushed Scott’s ERA to 2.91. “Today I think was just an odd day.”
Four pitches later, the game was over. Stewart came in to face the pinch-hitting Ramírez, but grooved him a fastball that was launched to left for the walk-off blast.
“It was supposed to be up above the zone. That’s where my fastball plays best,” Stewart said. “Just missed my spot, threw it right down the middle.”
Thus, the Dodgers suffered a loss that wasted big days from Emmet Sheehan (who threw six scoreless innings in his start) and Josue De Paula (who mashed a monstrous three-run home run in the fourth inning for his first career hit), while also delaying any possibility of clinching a playoff spot for a second-straight day.
“It’s baseball,” Roberts said. “It sucks. It feels bad. But that’s part of the thing.”
With a sigh, he later added: “But yeah, today was a crappy one.”
